title: China’s Xpeng targets overseas robotaxi trials next year, wider rollout in 2 to 3 years
source_used: CNA (interview with Xpeng vice-chairman and president Brian Gu)
key_facts: Xpeng plans to begin testing robotaxis in selected overseas cities next year, vice-chairman and president Brian Gu told CNA at the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore.
Gu said larger-scale commercial deployment of robotaxis around the world could come two to three years later; he did not name the cities.
Xpeng is testing its Yoyo robotaxi in Guangzhou with close to 100 vehicles in the pilot.
Xpeng's driver-assistance systems were used for nearly 60 per cent of the distance travelled by its vehicles; fully autonomous robotaxis need a higher bar, Gu said.
Xpeng is preparing to produce its 1.73 m humanoid robot Iron in larger quantities from early next year.
Iron will first work in Xpeng's own stores and offices as a receptionist and sales assistant; Xpeng intends to offer it to external customers in the second half of 2027.
quote_evidence: “Starting next year, we hope to launch pilot testing in select global cities,” Gu told CNA on the sidelines of the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore.
Xpeng is currently testing its Yoyo robotaxi in the southern Chinese city of Guangzhou, with close to 100 vehicles involved in the pilot.
Xpeng intends to begin offering Iron to external customers in the second half of 2027, he added.
why_it_matters_hint: Xpeng's executive gives a timetable for taking driverless taxis abroad, but names no cities and calls it a hope.
notes: Continues our 9 Oct 2026 entry on the Yoyo invitation-only trials. What is new: the overseas pilot timetable, the roughly 100-vehicle Guangzhou pilot and the Iron robot plans. Page text includes site menus, not used.
